title: Spread a Noetherian fibre-regular principal quotient to a flat basic neighbourhood
statement: Let $A_0\to B_0$ be a flat [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map] finitely presented [def-weil-pbc-finitely-presented-algebra] map of Noetherian commutative rings [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring]. Let $\mathfrak q_0\subset B_0$ be a prime ideal, $\mathfrak p_0$ its contraction to $A_0$, and $a_0\in\mathfrak q_0$. Suppose the image of $a_0$ is a regular singleton [def-weil-pbc-regular-sequence] in the closed-fibre local ring $C_0=(B_0)_{\mathfrak q_0}/\mathfrak p_0(B_0)_{\mathfrak q_0}$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime]. Then $(B_0)_{\mathfrak q_0}/(a_0)$ is flat over $(A_0)_{\mathfrak p_0}$ and over $A_0$, and there exists $g_0\in B_0\setminus\mathfrak q_0$ such that $H_0=(B_0)_{g_0}/(a_0)$ is flat over $A_0$ [def-weil-ring-localization-away].

source.place: Tag 056Y, label lemma-slice-given-element, proof, last paragraph: Grothendieck local flatness and openness for the principal quotient (old steps 8–9).

proof.text: Put $R=(A_0)_{\mathfrak p_0}$ and $S=(B_0)_{\mathfrak q_0}$. The flat-local-ring-maps lemma applied to the given flat map $A_0\to B_0$ and the prime $\mathfrak q_0$ says that $R\to S$ is flat and local, and that both local rings are Noetherian. Its maximal source ideal is $\mathfrak p_0R$, and its extension to $S$ is $\mathfrak p_0S$; hence its closed fibre is exactly the specified ring $C_0$.

source.place: Tag 056Y, label lemma-slice-given-element, proof, final paragraph; flat quotient part only.

proof.text: Use the Grothendieck regular-sequence theorem for $R\to S$, with $c=1$ and $f_1=a_0/1$. The closed-fibre regular-sequence hypothesis is precisely the assumed regular singleton in $C_0=S/\mathfrak p_0S$. For $i=1$ the theorem gives $Q=S/(a_0/1)$ flat over $R$. This is the first asserted local quotient.

source.place: Tag 056Y, label lemma-slice-given-element, proof, final paragraph; flat quotient part only.

proof.text: As an $R$-module, $Q$ is flat over $A_0$ by the flat-over-localization equivalence for $A_0\to R$. Put $T=B_0/(a_0)$ and let $\overline{\mathfrak q}_0=\mathfrak q_0/(a_0)\subset T$, which is prime because $T/\overline{\mathfrak q}_0=B_0/\mathfrak q_0$ is a domain. The quotient-localization isomorphism $S/(a_0/1)\cong T_{\overline{\mathfrak q}_0}$ sends $[b/s]$ to $\bar b/\bar s$. It preserves the $A_0$-action since it sends each base element to its class. Thus $T_{\overline{\mathfrak q}_0}$ is flat over $A_0$, proving also the second asserted local flatness.

source.place: Tag 056Y, label lemma-slice-given-element, proof, final paragraph; flat quotient part only.

proof.text: The algebra $T$ is finitely presented over $A_0$: take a finite polynomial presentation for $B_0$ and append to its finite list of relations a polynomial lifting $a_0$. As a $T$-module, $T$ has presentation $T^0\to T\xrightarrow{1}T\to0$. Apply openness of flatness to $A_0\to T$ and the module $T$. The resulting open flat locus contains $\overline{\mathfrak q}_0$ by the preceding step. The basic-open basis gives $\gamma\in T\setminus\overline{\mathfrak q}_0$ such that every prime $\mathfrak r$ avoiding $\gamma$ has $T_{\mathfrak r}$ flat over $A_0$. Lift $\gamma$ to $g_0\in B_0$; then $g_0\notin\mathfrak q_0$.

source.place: Tag 056Y, label lemma-slice-given-element, proof, final paragraph; flat quotient part only.

proof.text:
Write $H=T_\gamma$. For any prime $P\subset H$, let $\mathfrak r$ be its contraction to $T$. Since $\gamma$ is a unit in $H$, $\gamma
otin\mathfrak r$. There is a $T$-algebra isomorphism $H_P\cong T_{\mathfrak r}$: the forward map sends $(s/\gamma^n)/(t/\gamma^m)$ to $s\gamma^m/(t\gamma^n)$, and the inverse sends $s/t$ to $(s/1)/(t/1)$. Indeed $t/\gamma^m
otin P$ iff $t
otin\mathfrak r$, so all displayed denominators are units. The localization universal property constructs both maps; their composites fix $T$ and the inverted denominators, hence are identities by uniqueness. They fix $A_0$ through $T$.

source.place: Tag 056Y, label lemma-slice-given-element, proof, final paragraph; flat quotient part only.

proof.text: For each prime $P\subset H$, the preceding identification makes $H_P$ flat over $A_0$, because its contraction $\mathfrak r$ avoids $\gamma$ and lies in the flat locus chosen in step 4. Let $\mathfrak p$ be the contraction of $P$ to $A_0$. All elements of $A_0\setminus\mathfrak p$ are units in $H_P$, so its scalar action factors through $(A_0)_{\mathfrak p}$. The flat-over-localization equivalence makes $H_P$ flat over $(A_0)_{\mathfrak p}$. Applying the flat-map local criterion to $A_0\to H$ now gives $H$ flat over $A_0$.

source.place: Tag 056Y, label lemma-slice-given-element, proof, final paragraph; flat quotient part only.

proof.text: Finally, quotient and principal localization commute: with $J=(a_0)\subset B_0$ and $b=g_0$, the cited isomorphism identifies $H=(B_0/(a_0))_\gamma$ with $(B_0)_{g_0}/(a_0)$ by $\bar x/\gamma^n\mapsto[x/g_0^n]$. This is $A_0$-linear since both base actions factor through $B_0$ and the displayed map fixes its image. Therefore the flatness of $H$ gives exactly the required flatness of $H_0$, with the already chosen $g_0\notin\mathfrak q_0$.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q78-64d8264b5 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read the full item, all seven steps and the full statement of every cited node. The delivery adds a seven-step proof to a node that previously had only a statement; it adds no new nodes and does not change the statement. There is no repair note for this item, so the re-split rule does not apply. The statement is exactly the flat-quotient part of Stacks Tag 056Y, last paragraph (more-morphisms.tex l.6166-6262): Grothendieck local flatness, then openness of flatness. It is not weakened, and the parent lem-trf-fibre-regular-element-flat-hypersurface step 4 uses exactly these hypotheses and this conclusion. Step checks: (1) flat-local-ring-maps gives R=(A0)_p0 -> S=(B0)_q0 flat, local and Noetherian, with closed fibre S/p0S = C0. (2) The Grothendieck regular-sequence lemma with c=1 and i=1 gives S/(a0) flat over R. (3) The flat-over-localization equivalence gives flatness over A0, and localization-at-prime-of-quotient gives Q = T_qbar with the base action kept. (4) T=B0/(a0) is finitely presented over A0 (append a lift of a0 to a presentation of B0) and T is a finitely presented T-module. Openness of flatness for A0->T with M=T, plus the basic-open basis, gives gamma not in qbar, lifted to g0 not in q0. (5) H_P = T_r through two universal-property maps; the argument holds with zero divisors. (6) Flat-over-localization and the flat-map local criterion give H flat over A0; this fills in the passage Stacks leaves implicit. (7) Localization-quotient-commute gives H = (B0)_g0/(a0), compatibly with A0. Small cases: Z[t] at (p,t) with a0=t and with a0=t+p works. k[s,t] at (s,t) with a0=st fails the hypothesis, and B/(st) really is not flat. Duplicate search over the DAG (056Y, fibre-regular, flat quotient and openness) found no node stating the same result. lem-pur-fiber-regular-sequence-neighbourhood concludes regularity, not flatness of the quotient, and the sfb slice-flat nodes are at scheme/space level and cite the parent chain. Accepted tool_uses: the Grothendieck regular-sequence lemma (Stacks 00MG) and openness of flatness (Stacks 00RC). Both are generic commutative-algebra black boxes, used as in the 056Y proof. No SGA source is used. No fixes.
